market.headline: Chip stocks are dragging tech lower before the open: QQQ is at 673.7, below its 200-day average of 680.94. Nvidia's CEO exit and fears of tougher China chip rules are behind the selling, and the 08:30 PPI print sets the tone on rates.
watch: 08:30 PPI: a monthly change above 0.65% is hot, below 0.47% is cool
QQQ close vs 680.94 (200-day average): this decides whether to cut
SPY 733.0 below (decline continuing) and 764.43 above (add level)
market.if_then: If QQQ closes below 680.94, then trim QQQ and chip exposure into the close; if PPI is cool and QQQ closes back above 680.94, then keep existing exposure and add nothing until it closes above 718.46.

stocks.headline: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO amid a spy scandal. The stock is at 159.98 before the open, down 3.7% after falling 4.3% to 166.19 yesterday on 4.5 times normal volume.
stocks.why: The business has not broken: sales are up 106%, the operating margin is 65%, and next year's profit forecasts rose 24% in 90 days. The stock trades at 10 times next year's earnings, its cheapest in five years. The danger is political. Huang backed keeping China sales open, and Commerce Secretary Lutnick will now testify to the Senate about China chip sales, so tougher export rules are a real threat to sales. Brokers are cutting targets (Melius to 185, DA Davidson to 200). Nvidia reports around Nov 17 with no CEO in place, so the whole AI chip and AI-cloud group trades on its headlines until then.

long_term.reason: This agrees with the house view. The business is very strong and the stock is cheap, but there is no successor, China rules are unknown and earnings are four days out. Buy after the report, not before it.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A named permanent CEO, plus Nov 17 guidance that holds up on China, turns this into a Buy.
stocks.action: Don't buy the open. Hold what you own, add nothing before the Nov 17 report, and treat 148.80 as the line that must hold.

levels.means: Above = sellers are exhausted and the stock can rally into earnings. Below = the stock is still under pressure from the scandal.
Above = yesterday's panic low holds. Below = no floor; stay out until after earnings.

stocks.if_then: If it breaks below 148.80, then cut any trading position and wait for the Nov 17 report before rebuilding.

stocks.headline: AMD is down 9.7% before the open at 528.4, giving back part of a 44.7% five-day run with no company news.
stocks.why: AMD ran as the alternative to Nvidia, so it falls hardest when the group sells off on fears of tougher China chip rules. The business is strong: sales are up 45% and speeding up, the operating margin doubled to 18%, and profit forecasts rose 15% in 90 days. But the stock still trades at 126 times last year's profit. Price is the problem, not the company. If it breaks the 20-day average, the run unwinds further and drags ARM and SMCI with it.

long_term.reason: This agrees with the house view. The business is excellent, but the price ran far ahead of it in a week. Better entries come after this shakeout.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A hold above 518.76 through the Nvidia report with steady estimates would make it an Add on dips.
stocks.action: Don't buy the drop. Revisit only if it closes above 518.76 today. If you bought during the run, sell a third if it breaks 518.76.

levels.means: Above = the dip gets bought and the run resumes. Below = the giveback continues.
Above = a normal pullback inside the uptrend. Below = the run is unwinding; expect more selling.

stocks.if_then: If it trades below 518.76, then trim a third of any position bought during the run.

stocks.headline: CoreWeave is down 12.3% before the open at 49.65, wiping out most of its post-earnings jump.
stocks.why: The Nov 10 report beat on sales growth (up 168%), but the company still loses money: a quarterly loss of 1.27 per share and a negative operating margin. It carries 24.9B of debt against 4.1B of cash. Its 132.3B backlog is real, but it is paid for with borrowed money. The worry that Nvidia's leadership crisis spills into the AI financing boom lands hardest on borrowers like this. A break below its pre-earnings price says the market has rejected the report.

long_term.reason: The house view does not judge it long-term and avoids it for swing trades. Losses plus heavy debt make it the weakest link if AI funding tightens.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A path to positive operating profit, or debt refinanced on easy terms, would move it to Wait.
stocks.action: Don't buy. If you hold it, sell into any bounce toward 55.4.

levels.means: Above = the selling was a one-day shakeout. Below = the trend stays down.
Above = some of the earnings gain survives. Below = the earnings jump is fully erased; exit.

stocks.if_then: If it trades below 48.98, then sell every remaining share.
